title: Redwood POC Weekly Sync - Benchmark Review vs Baseline Provider
summary: Weekly POC sync to review Redwood vs baseline provider benchmarks. Redwood presented per-model latency and throughput numbers using current batching and KV caching; SE proposed tuning and quant profiles. Customer raised concerns about tail latency on short prompts and throughput consistency under steady state. Agreed next steps: share raw benchmark spreadsheet, run dedicated GPU comparison in VPC, tune batching and re-run, customer to share representative input distribution and SLOs.
action_items: Alex Chen | Send per-model benchmarking spreadsheet + raw logs | 2025-03-14
Priya Patel | Tune batching config (dynamic batch windows) and re-run CPU/GPU tests | 2025-03-18
Priya Patel | Re-run KV-cache-on and KV-cache-off experiments and export tail latency percentiles | 2025-03-18
Samira Khan | Provide sample input distribution file and target p50/p95/p99 SLOs | 2025-03-15
Liam O'Connor | Provision VPC peering for dedicated on-prem trial and confirm networking windows | 2025-03-17
next_steps: Alex to upload full benchmark spreadsheet and graphs to shared Drive
Schedule dedicated run in BrightMetrics VPC next week (AE/SE + SRE)
SE to propose quantization profile and expected cost delta
Customer to confirm pilot success criteria and timeline for expansion
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-03-12 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45 mins. Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (Redwood CSM) | BrightMetrics: Samira Khan (Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Infra), Daniel Park (Product), Nina Zhou (SRE).

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick agenda | benchmark review, tuning suggestions, next steps. we did the run versus the baseline provider last week and priya will walk through the numbers.
[00:20] Priya: yeah hi all, so we ran the baseline (they call it BaselineCloud) and our Redwood Dedicated profile on the same instance types where possible, same model checkpoints. quick note, transcription or notes in the spreadsheet, some names might be a little off.
[00:35] Priya: first slide | p50/p95/p99 for generation on short prompts (<=64 tokens). Baseline p50 ~ 45 ms, p95 ~ 210 ms, p99 ~ 480 ms. Redwood p50 ~ 38 ms, p95 ~ 160 ms, p99 ~ 410 ms. so we're about 10-20% better on median and ~20% on tail in this config.
[01:05] Samira: okay that's promising, but our concern is those p99 numbers | we need consistency at p95 for latency sensitive features, p99 is less critical but still matters. how were you measuring | single connection or multi-connection?
[01:20] Priya: good question | tests were multiclient load (50 concurrent clients) to simulate heavy web traffic. we also ran a steady-state throughput test at 200 rps for 30 minutes which i'll show.
[01:35] Priya: throughput | baseline achieved ~1.8k tokens/sec aggregate, Redwood ~2.1k tokens/sec with same batch settings. when we enabled KV cache for multi-turn flows, effective token throughput improved by ~25% on Redwood because of cache hits. note: baseline had a KV cache implementation but it was less effective in our workload due to missing prefix deduping.
[02:05] Liam: when you say KV cache, are you talking about prefix caching or full key-value attention cache, like in the runtime? our worry is cache coherency across nodes | how does Redwood handle that in Dedicated?
[02:20] Priya: good catch | this is local KV cache per-gpu shard with sticky routing on the serving layer. in Dedicated we can pin sessions to a pool so cache hits are high. there's a fallback to cold start if the sticky routing misses, but for web scale we see >85% hit rates in our run.
[02:45] Nina: network jitter was a factor in our infra | did you account for VPC egress and cross-zone latency in the test?
[02:55] Priya: the public tests were done in the same AZ to keep network variance low; we did a smaller run across zones and saw p95 increase by ~12%. for the VPC test we'll want to run inside the customer's VPC to capture true cross-zone behavior.
[03:15] Daniel: can you walk through batching config? our baseline uses a pretty aggressive batching window to favor throughput, but we need a balance for short-latency calls.
[03:30] Priya: sure | current Redwood config used dynamic batching with 8-12 ms batch windows and a max batch size of 64. we also applied per-model sequence length heuristics to avoid padding too much. baseline was using a 20 ms static window which increased throughput but hurt short prompt latency.
[03:55] Alex: to add, we suggested a hybrid profile: small window (6 ms) for low-latency endpoints and a throughput profile for batch jobs. that can be routed by API route or header.
[04:10] Samira: okay, does Redwood support on-the-fly routing rules? meaning can we send a header to choose the latency-optimized pool?
[04:20] Alex: yes, you can set a route parameter or tag traffic at the SDK level and Redwood's smart router will pick the appropriate pool. we also have automatic fallback to cheaper pools if the primary is saturated.
[04:30] Daniel: what's the cost delta if we move to the low-latency pool versus baseline provider? we need rough economics.
[04:40] Maria: we have a costing model in the spreadsheet | ballpark we estimate 18-25% lower per-token cost for the Redwood config once you factor KV cache hits and batching efficiency; the baseline had higher overhead for padding and less effective cache. we'll send the per-model numbers.
[05:05] Samira: that's helpful. one of our internal concerns is quantization: we need to preserve output quality. did you run int8 or other quant profiles in this benchmark?
[05:20] Priya: current run was fp16 on both sides for parity. we ran a separate quant test | int8 dynamic | which reduced memory footprint and increased throughput ~30% but there was a small regression in semantic consistency on some edge prompt sets. we can share eval diffs.
[05:40] Samira: yes please, we want eval diffs | we have a set of 120 prompts that matter, if you could run those under quant profiles that'd help.
[05:50] Priya: noted | we'll run the 120 prompt eval and include BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics and a manual spot check.
[06:00] Liam: also, tail latency | can you provide p99.9? baseline numbers for p99.9 were spiking to ~900-1,200 ms occasionally, which is concerning for our interactive UI.
[06:15] Priya: we captured p99.9 | baseline peaked ~1.1s, Redwood peaked ~920 ms in this test. spikes correlated with garbage collection events on the baseline's runtime and occasionally network jitter. in our Dedicated config GC is controlled and we saw fewer spikes.
[06:35] Samira: how repeatable are these numbers? we need confidence before committing to expansion.
[06:45] Alex: repeatability was tested via three independent runs at different times of day; variance was low for median but tail variance persisted; that's why next step is to run inside BrightMetrics VPC and run a longer 4-hour steady-state to capture long-tail behaviors.
[07:05] Nina: regarding security/compliance for the VPC run, we'll need the SSO and audit log samples and any SOC2 attestation. can you share the security docs?
[07:20] Alex: yes, Maria will share SOC2 and the audit log format. we also have KMS integration for key management.
[07:30] Maria: sending docs after the call, and I'll include an example audit timeline.
[07:38] Samira: good. also curious about model version pinning, if we pin a model and Redwood upgrades, what's the rollback story?
[07:50] Priya: you can pin model versions per-route. rollouts are canary by default | you can do A/B and automatic rollback if quality metrics degrade. we also store model hashes and can revert to an earlier binary within the Dedicated pool.
[08:10] Daniel: during the benchmark, did you simulate multi-tenant noisy neighbor scenarios? our concern is that under resource contention results degrade.
[08:25] Priya: yes for the public test we ran a noisy neighbor job on separate GPU hosts. Redwood Dedicated isolated the pilot into a reserved pool and didn't exhibit the same degradation; baseline with shared tenancy had throughput drop ~17% under noisy neighbor load.
[08:45] Samira: that's an important point. do you have SLA numbers for Dedicated throughput guarantees?
[08:55] Alex: we can provide SLA language for Dedicated capacity | Maria will include that in the package. typically we commit to throughput and latency targets for reserved pools with monitoring and credits for breaches.
[09:10] Samira: okay. on the instrumentation side, can we get token-level traces and cost breakdown per-request? that's crucial for our internal chargeback.
[09:25] Maria: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns; we'll provide a sample export from the pilot dataset.
[09:35] Priya: back to tuning | recommended immediate changes: reduce batch window to 6 ms for low-latency routes, enable kv sticky routing by session id, and use model-specific quant profiles for background jobs. we expect p95 to drop ~15% with these changes.
[09:55] Liam: about quant again, we need to see the semantics regression on our 120 prompts before we accept int8 on production. can you run that and share diffs?
[10:05] Priya: yes, will include diffs and a short manual review summary.
[10:12] Samira: what's the plan for the VPC dedicated run timeline?
[10:18] Alex: propose next Wednesday 2025-03-19 for the inside-VPC dedicated benchmark | will require provisioning from your infra. Liam, can you confirm availability?
[10:28] Liam: likely yes, need to check scheduled maintenance but tentatively ok. I'll confirm by Friday.
[10:34] Daniel: if we move forward after VPC run, what's the minimum commitment for Dedicated?
[10:40] Alex: Dedicated has monthly reserved capacity | we can start with a small pilot pool and scale; specifics depend on throughput commitments, but we often do a 3-month pilot for production evaluation.
[10:50] Samira: let's make the pilot success criteria explicit | p95 < 250 ms for short prompts, p99 < 500 ms for interactive surfaces, throughput >= 2k tokens/sec for our steady-state job.
[11:05] Alex: noted | we'll confirm if those are achievable after the VPC run and tuning.
[11:12] Priya: one more note | for the baseline we found inefficiencies in padding due to variable sequence lengths; Redwood's per-model sequence heuristics reduced average token padding by ~12% which helped cost.
[11:30] Samira: ok, that'll factor into unit economics. please show per-model breakdown in the spreadsheet.
[11:38] Alex: will do. any other questions?
[11:42] Daniel: quick one | do you support in-line function/tool calls in the runtime, and does that affect latency? baseline has a tool-calling integration that adds 30-60 ms on average.
[11:55] Priya: yes, Redwood supports function calling and structured output. tool-call overhead depends on the external call but the runtime can do async prefetching; typical overhead is 20-40 ms if you prewarm routes. we'll include measurements.
[12:12] Samira: awesome. thanks everyone. recap of next steps?
[12:18] Alex: recap: 1) Alex/Maria upload full benchmark spreadsheet + logs by 2025-03-14, 2) Priya to tune batching and re-run tests and quant evals by 2025-03-18, 3) BrightMetrics to provide sample distribution + confirm VPC peering details by 2025-03-15/17, 4) run inside-VPC benchmark week of 2025-03-19, 5) follow-up call after VPC run.
[12:45] Samira: good, we'll look for the spreadsheet. thanks.
[12:50] Alex: thanks all | meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcript contains typical speech artifacts, slightly imperfect naming (BaselineCloud spelled as baselinecloth in one export), and occasional filler words. The raw spreadsheet referenced: link placeholder: https://drive.example.com/redwood/poc/brightmetrics/benchmarks.
